content: If you are using this medication at home, it is essential to learn all preparation and usage instructions from your healthcare professional. The solution should appear clear and light yellow. Before use, visually inspect the product for any particles or discoloration. If you notice either, do not use the liquid. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, constipation, or anxiety. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to ceftazidime, avibactam, penicillins, beta-lactam antibiotics, other cephalosporins, or beta-lactamase inhibitors (e.g., sulbactam), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ceftazidime/avibactam may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Ceftazidime passes into breast milk, but it is unknown if avibactam does. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., Coombs' test, urine glucose tests), potentially causing false results. In case of overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function) should be performed while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
